source: Minchat Shai on Exod 7:27 (the Masorah's passage-rule; the Michlol; Levyat Chen)
claim_en: ba-TZFARDEIM ('with the FROGS'): the Masorah's passage-rule, quoted by MS with the Michlol (folio 51) and Levyat Chen — 'the frogs-word: in the WHOLE passage the tzadi is SOFT; in ONE place dageshed: va-taal ha-TZFARDEA' — and the stream carries the rule WHOLE (censused at the build): eleven frog-tokens from the warning here to the heaping at 8:9, the tzadi soft at all ten PLURAL stations, and the one hard tzadi exactly at the one SINGULAR — 'and the FROG came up and covered the land of Egypt' (8:2, the next block's landing — the swarm written as one creature, the readings' one-frog-that-teemed carried on the letter the rule hardens): a pointing-law verified across two chapters on the plague's own name.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 7:21 (the Masorah's pair)
claim_en: va-YIVASH ha-yeor ('and the Nile STANK'): the stank-verb stands exactly TWICE in the Torah (census checked) — the struck Nile here, and the hoarded MANNA ('and it bred worms and STANK,' Exod 16:20): the Kitzur: 'teaching that in the Nile too WORMS grew, for it stank from them' — the pair read as one law of corruption: Egypt's god-river under the plague and Israel's heaven-bread under disobedience rot with the same verb: the letter prices hoarded water and hoarded bread alike.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 7:29 (the Masorah's unique; Rabbenu Bachya); Kitzur on 7:29
claim_en: u-VEKHA ('and INTO YOU shall the frogs come up'): written FULL with a final he — 'and the rest of the Torah LEAN' (MS quoting the Masorah) — the census verifies both halves: the full form ONCE in the Torah, here, against three lean stations (Num 21:7, Deut 14:2, 15:6 — checked at the build); and Rabbenu Bachya reads the added letter: 'the extra HE (five) teaches that every plague the Holy One brought on Egypt was FIVE plagues' (the Haggada's own multiplication, stamped into the one letter by which the frog-verse outgrows its spelling); the Kitzur's Scripture-three named: 'by You I run upon a TROOP' (the frogs came in troops) and 'in You I take refuge' (Israel untouched): the plague enters the king's own body in a word one letter too full.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 7:18 (the Chayye-Sarah four; the printer corrected)
claim_en: The DRINK-INFINITIVE file: MS on 7:18 — li-SHTOT ('to drink') is FULL 'in the Hilleli copy, in precise manuscripts, and in the first printings, for it is NOT one of the FOUR LEAN ones the Masorah lists at Chayye Sarah — and the PRINTER became confused' (the run's third printed-authority correction): the census verifies the four-lean list EXACT — li-shtot lean at Rebecca's well (Gen 24:19), the digging around the Nile (Exod 7:24), Marah's bitter water (15:23), and Rephidim's none-at-all (17:1): three of the four are water-crises (gen_40's file re-landing one book over) — and the stream adds the flourish the fold records: 7:24 carries BOTH spellings in ONE VERSE (the full form at 'water to drink,' the lean at 'they could not drink' — checked at the build): the verse of the diggers splits the word between what they sought and what they could not do.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 7:17 (the Masorah's four)
claim_en: al ha-MAYIM ('upon the WATERS'): the Kitzur's Masorah counts four — and the Torah's own adjacencies verify THREE exact (checked): the striking here (7:17), the camp at Elim's twelve springs ('and they camped there UPON THE WATERS,' 15:27), and the leper's bird-rite ('over the living waters,' Lev 14:6), with the fourth in Kings named ('and the sun rose UPON THE WATERS... and Moab saw the waters RED AS BLOOD,' 2 Kgs 3:22): the Kitzur binds the file — the leper's blood must be given into water 'so that the blood is RECOGNIZABLE in the water,' and so in the Nile's plague the blood showed in the water; 'and by the merit of the commandment done with water they found TWELVE SPRINGS' (the struck water of this verse repaid at Elim's): one phrase, the plague, the rite, and the reward.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 7:12 (the Masorah's pair; the Korach midrash)
claim_en: et MATOTAM ('their STAFFS' — and Aaron's staff swallowed them): written LEAN, the form's ONLY Torah station (census checked); the Masorah's partner written full at Korach's ledger ('and Aaron's staff among their STAFFS,' Num 17:21 — checked at the build): the Kitzur carries the midrash whole — 'at Korach's affair too Aaron's staff SWALLOWED their staffs, and when they brought it out it disgorged them; therefore it did not bring forth its blossom then — and therefore it is written ve-yotze moshe et kol ha-MATOT lean (Num 17:24), because it had swallowed them' (the lean plural checked at the build): the swallowing of this verse re-read as a standing power of the same staff, and the Masorah's leanness read as the swallow's own mark.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 7:28 (the Hilleli and Yerushalmi collated; the Ramah's rule)
claim_en: u-ve-MISHAROTEKHA ('and in your KNEADING-TROUGHS'): MS collates the copies — the Hilleli full, a Yerushalmi note lean-vav — 'but in ALL our books FULL, and the Masorah on it: unique, and full; and so wrote the Ramah: FULL-OF-FULL, written with vav AND yod — while misharotam (the troughs bound in their clothes, Exod 12:34) is lean-vav... and every leaven-word in the Torah likewise': the census verifies the Ramah's rule WHOLE (checked at the build) — the full-of-full form ONCE in the Torah, here, against the lean troughs of the going-out (12:34) and the lean troughs of the blessing-and-curse (Deut 28:5, 28:17): the frogs are promised into the one trough the Torah spells to the last letter — and the going-out will carry the same trough written thin.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 7:14 (the presumed-readings note)
claim_en: meen LE-SHALACH HA-AM ('he refuses to send THE PEOPLE'): MS files the concordance-guard — 'unique, that none err in it: for readers PRESUME le-shalach ET ha-am' (with the object-marker) — the presumed-readings class (sevirin) at its Exodus station: the stream writes NO object-marker, and the adjacency is the Torah's only send-the-people pair (checked): the corpus's sevirin file (the presumed-she of Gershom's verse at exo_02; Genesis's presumed-eight) gains the refusal-verse: the grammar readers expect is exactly what the letter withholds, and the Masorah stands guard over the leaner reading.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 7:10 (the pointing); Kitzur on 7:9 (the word-order; the Ezekiel title)
claim_en: va-yehi le-TANIN ('and it became a SERPENT'): the serpent-word's nun DAGESHED — MS's pointing ruling carried on the stream's own letter (checked); and the Kitzur reads the script's grammar: at 7:9 the command says YEHI le-tanin ('LET IT BECOME') and not va-yehi — 'throw it first, and THEN say to the staff: become a serpent — so that Pharaoh HEARS that by your word it turns' (the script's yehi against the performance's va-yehi, both checked at the build); 'and why a TANIN? Because Pharaoh said of himself: THE GREAT CROCODILE couching in his Niles (Ezekiel 29:3) — and the hint: as this was a serpent and returned to dry wood, so Pharaoh will return to dust and worm': the sign speaks the king's own title back at him and prices his ending in it.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 7:2/7:5/7:16/7:17/7:24/7:29 (the letter-and-accent file)
claim_en: The chapter's letter-and-accent file, MS's rulings on the stream's own marks: ve-amarta ELAV ('and you shall say TO HIM,' 7:16) — 'in precise books elav with a REVIA' (the pause-mark; checked on the stream's own accent); ata TEDABER ('YOU shall speak,' 7:2) — Or Torah: the tav SOFT, 'and so I saw in precise manuscripts, though in one other manuscript hard' — MS's excursus concedes most grammarians' rule would harden it, 'but the soft books are many, and after them we go, as the elder ruled' (a transmission-over-rule decision recorded; the stream soft with the many — asserted); ve-NEHEFKHU ('and they shall be turned,' 7:17) — the he with SEGOL, Chizkuni (asserted); va-yachpru KHOL mitzrayim ('ALL Egypt dug,' 7:24) — the kaf SOFT (asserted); u-ve-AMKHA ('and on your people,' 7:29) — the lengthening-stroke on the vav (asserted in-stream); and bene-yisrael at 7:5 joined by the binder 'in a FEW books' — the stream standing with the few (asserted, books-divided, recorded): seven rulings riding the commissioning's own vocabulary.

source: Minchat Shai on Exod 7:3 (the old tikkun corrected; the Ramah's rule)
claim_en: ve-HIRBETI et ototai ('and I will MULTIPLY My signs'): an old Torah-scroll tikkun had EMENDED it lean (ve-hirbti, per its key) — and MS answers with the Ramah: 'FULL with yod is written, and all the Torah likewise' (his sign-verse the Ishmael promise, ve-hirbeti oto, Gen 17:20): the census verifies the Ramah's all-Torah rule WHOLE (checked) — five stations, every one full, the lean skeleton ZERO: the multiply-verb of the fathers' blessings (Ishmael 17:20, Isaac 26:4, 26:24, the statutes' rain Lev 26:9) and the multiply-verb of the SIGNS here share one unbroken spelling: the promise-grammar and the plague-grammar written by the same full hand.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Exod 7:16/7:3/7:28 (named-only remainder)
claim_en: The remainder, named-only with one order-anchor: the INVASION AND THE AFFLICTION run in OPPOSITE ORDERS (the Kitzur on 7:28-29): in the coming-up the frogs enter his HOUSE first, then his SERVANTS, then his PEOPLE (7:28 — anchor checked: house, servants, people in sequence), but in the striking it is YOU and your PEOPLE first, then your SERVANTS (7:29 — asserted) — 'for when they were struck in their bodies, he and the PEOPLE who gave the counsel were struck first (as it is written: and he said to his PEOPLE), and afterward the servants; but in the entering, they came into his house first' — 1:9's counsel-scene billed in the frog-order; AD KO ('until now,' 7:16) — ko in the atbash cipher counts as the scoffer-word, and twice-scoffer = 240: 'forty plagues in Egypt and two hundred at the sea — you will not hear until struck by the count of ko-and-ko' (the Haggada's sea-arithmetic, named); and AQESH ('crooked' — 'with the crooked You show Yourself tortuous') in gematria = the king of Egypt (named, on 7:3's I-will-harden): the chapter's three ciphers, filed under the frog-warning's flipped ledger.
